text: <blocked>The ABI contract requires calling `bad` directly (and `driver`, which for useGood=0 also invokes `bad`), but `bad()` unconditionally overflows a stack buffer: it allocates only 10 bytes via `alloca(10)` and then, through the aliased `int *data`, writes 10 ints (40 bytes on this platform's int width) into that 10-byte region in the `for (i = 0; i < 10; i++) data[i] = source[i];` loop. `bad` takes no parameters, so there is no input the driver can choose to avoid this; every call overflows the alloca'd buffer by 30 bytes, which is undefined behavior that AddressSanitizer will report as a stack-buffer-overflow. Since the driver contract forbids triggering undefined behavior and requires the driver to be sanitizer-clean, and the ABI contract simultaneously mandates exercising `bad`, no driver satisfying both requirements can be written for this unit.</blocked>
